preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 10 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 1000 and 1 <= m <= n for n, m in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is between 2 and 1000, and m is between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(all(0 <= a <= 10000 for a in weights) for weights in test_cases_weights)
preconditions.description: For each test case, all fridge weights are integers between 0 and 10000 inclusive.

postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either a single line containing -1, or a line with the minimum cost followed by exactly m lines describing the chains.

postconditions.expression: all((u != v and 1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n) for u, v in chains)
postconditions.description: Every chain connects two distinct fridges with valid indices between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(all(degree[i] >= 1 for i in range(n)) for chains in valid_solutions)
postconditions.description: In any valid solution, every fridge must have at least one chain connected to it (degree >= 1), ensuring no other person can open it alone.

postconditions.expression: total_cost == sum(a[u-1] + a[v-1] for u, v in chains)
postconditions.description: The reported total cost equals the sum of weights of the two fridges for each chain in the solution.
The solution provided minimizes the total cost among all valid configurations of m chains that satisfy the privacy constraint.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == '-1' if m < n else False
postconditions.description: If m is less than n, no solution exists because at least n chains are required to ensure every fridge has degree >= 1, so output must be -1.
